prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Dallas — the right provider depends on your needs (single tooth vs full-arch, bone grafting or sinus lift required, medical history, budget, timeline, sedation needs, etc.). I can help you find the best match. To start, here’s how to choose a top implant specialist and next steps you can take.

Who should place an implant
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons (OMFS) — surgical specialists for complex cases, extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, sedation/general anesthesia.
- Periodontists — specialists in the gums and supporting bone; many focus on implants.
- Prosthodontists — experts in the restorative/prosthetic portion (crowns, bridges, full-arch prostheses); often work with surgeons on complex reconstructions.
Look for an implant team where the surgical and restorative phases are coordinated.

Important credentials and experience
- Specialty training (OMFS, periodontics, prosthodontics) or fellowship in implant dentistry.
- Board certification or fellowship in AAOMS, ABO, AAID, ICOI or similar.
- Number of implants placed and experience with cases like yours (single vs full-arch, grafting, immediate loading).
- Use of modern technology: CBCT (3D imaging), guided implant planning/surgery, digital scans.
- Documented before/after photos and patient references.
- Clear complication and warranty policies.

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants do you place per year? How many similar to my case?
- Who will do the surgical and restorative work? Where will each phase be done?
- Will you use CBCT and digital planning? Do you offer guided surgery?
- Do I need bone grafting/sinus lift? If so, how often do you perform those?
- What are the risks, expected timeline, alternatives, and total cost (including restoration)?
- Can I see before/after photos of similar cases and contact patient references?

Where to search and verify
- AAOMS (oral surgeons) and American Academy of Periodontology directories.
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) and ICOI for implant-focused clinicians.
- Local reviews: Google, Healthgrades, Yelp — but weigh reviews with clinical credentials.
- Ask your general dentist for referrals and for the restorative dentist they prefer to work with on implants.

Red flags
- No clear written treatment plan or fees.
- Provider won’t show case photos or explain complication rates.
- No 3D imaging or unwillingness to coordinate with your restorative dentist.
- Promises of “lifetime” guarantees without clear terms.

If you want, I can:
- Look up highly rated implant specialists in Dallas if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood.
- Suggest a shortlist of specific practices (with credentials and contact details) and prep questions for your consults.

Which would you prefer — a shortlist for your area, or guidance tailored to your specific situation (single tooth vs multiple, bone issues, insurance)?
